term: "Generative Model"

## Simple explanation

A generative model learns patterns in data so it can produce new samples
that resemble the examples or follow a condition, such as a prompt.

## Technical explanation

A generative model may estimate a joint distribution $p(x)$, a
conditional distribution $p(x\mid c)$, or a mechanism for sampling data.
Model families include autoregressive models, diffusion models,
variational autoencoders, and GANs. Some models use implicit sampling
without a tractable likelihood.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Generative models power content creation, simulation, data synthesis,
and conditional completion. Their outputs require task-specific
evaluation because likelihood, realism, diversity, and usefulness are
different properties.

## How it works

The model learns from data using an architecture and objective, then
generates by sampling or iteratively transforming a latent input into
an output. Conditioning information can guide the sample toward a
requested category, context, or prompt.

## Practical example

A diffusion model can begin with a noise representation and iteratively
denoise it while using a text prompt as conditioning information to
generate an image.

## Common misconceptions

- A generative model does not necessarily memorize and replay training
  examples, though memorization should be assessed.
- A plausible sample is not necessarily true or representative.
- Not every model that outputs text is generative in the same technical
  sense; some systems select or retrieve existing content.
